analyticalQuestion: Does the exact fixed-charge s=-1 column admit an all-order monotonic endpoint theorem strong enough to close the reduced canonical restart at r=371/1000, and does the adjacent millesimal probe fail in the exact induced column rather than only in a separated upper bound?
supportedClaim: For s=-1, j>80, and j congruent to 1 modulo 3, the exact weighted column F_r(t), t=1/j, satisfies F'_r(t)>=3r-Qhat_r(1/82)>0 on 0<=t<=1/82. Its all-order maximum is therefore the true j=82 column. At r=371/1000 this column is 0.99722804122918895132 and every fixed-point and canonical-stretch gate passes. At r=372/1000 the same exact column is 1.0010616516434951437 and fails, while the common large-charge sector remains 0.97661386801873716684.

chartContract.takeaway: A uniform positive derivative bound makes j=82 the exact all-order s=-1 endpoint, turns r=0.371 into a strict pass, and identifies r=0.372 as an exact induced-column failure of the current sufficient norm.
chartContract.dataSufficiency: The formal derivative argument covers every admissible j>80 analytically. The 202 plotted curve samples and five finite lattice regressions are implementation and presentation checks rather than substitutes for the all-order theorem.
